pharm: Selective beta-2 agonist; activates adenylyl cyclase to relax airway smooth muscle
quick: 2 inhalations (90 mcg each) every 4-6 hours as needed for bronchospasm
Use only if potential benefit justifies risk; commonly used in pregnant asthmatics
Likely present in milk in small amounts; generally considered compatible
Symptom relief, frequency of use, heart rate, serum potassium, peak flow/FEV1
summary: Salbutamol (albuterol) is a short-acting selective beta-2 adrenergic agonist used as a quick-relief bronchodilator for the treatment and prevention of bronchospasm in reversible obstructive airway disease (asthma, COPD) and for prevention of exercise-induced bronchospasm. Onset is rapid, making it the standard rescue inhaler. Increasing need signals worsening disease control.
indications: Treatment or prevention of bronchospasm in adults and children aged 4 years and older with reversible obstructive airway disease
Prevention of exercise-induced bronchospasm in adults and children aged 4 years and older

dosage.d: 2 inhalations (90 mcg/actuation) every 4 to 6 hours; in some patients 1 inhalation every 4 hours may be sufficient
dosage.t: Shake and prime as directed; use a spacer if needed
dosage.n: More frequent use or increasing need indicates inadequate control
Not for routine maintenance alone in persistent asthma

dosage.d: 2.5 mg by nebulization 3 to 4 times daily, titrated to severity per product labeling
dosage.n: Doses individualized in acute severe asthma under supervision

admin: Prime the inhaler before first use, when not used for more than 2 weeks, or if dropped (release 4 sprays into the air, shaking before each)
Shake well before each actuation; coordinate actuation with a slow deep breath, or use a spacer
Clean the actuator with warm water at least once weekly and let it air-dry completely
Counsel patients that increasing reliance signals worsening asthma and the need for medical review
moa: Albuterol selectively activates beta-2 adrenergic receptors on airway smooth muscle. This stimulates adenylyl cyclase, increasing intracellular cyclic AMP, which activates protein kinase A, inhibits myosin phosphorylation, and lowers intracellular calcium. The result is relaxation of smooth muscle throughout the airways from the trachea to the terminal bronchioles, relieving bronchospasm. It also acts as a functional antagonist to bronchoconstrictor stimuli.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to albuterol or any component of the formulation
relative: Cardiovascular disorders, especially coronary insufficiency, arrhythmias, and hypertension
monitor: Serum potassium with high or frequent dosing
Asthma control and frequency of reliever use

preg: Available data have not shown a consistent drug-associated risk of major birth defects. Poorly controlled asthma in pregnancy carries maternal and fetal risk, and inhaled albuterol is commonly used. Use in pregnancy when the potential benefit justifies the potential risk; beta agonists may interfere with uterine contractility if used near term.
lact: Albuterol is likely present in human milk in small amounts after inhalation. Because of the low systemic exposure with inhaled use, it is generally considered compatible with breastfeeding; weigh benefits with the mother's clinical need.
renal: No specific dosage adjustment for renal impairment is provided in the labeling. Use the standard regimen with clinical monitoring.
hepatic: No specific dosage adjustment for hepatic impairment is provided in the labeling. Use the standard regimen with clinical monitoring.

major: Other short-acting sympathomimetic bronchodilators (additive cardiovascular effects; avoid concomitant excessive use)
Non-selective beta-blockers (block bronchodilation and may provoke severe bronchospasm)
moderate: Monoamine oxidase inhibitors and tricyclic antidepressants (potentiate cardiovascular effects; use with caution within 2 weeks)
minor: Drugs that lower potassium may have additive effects
interactions.food: Not applicable; administered by oral inhalation
interactions.diagnostics: May cause transient hypokalemia and elevated blood glucose; can affect ECG (QTc, T-wave changes) at high doses

serious: Significant cardiovascular effects (arrhythmias, marked tachycardia, hypertension)
emergency: Paradoxical bronchospasm immediately after dosing - stop and seek emergency care
Severe allergic reaction with swelling or difficulty breathing - emergency care
Severe chest pain or very fast/irregular heartbeat - emergency care

monitoring: Frequency of reliever use as a marker of asthma control
Symptom relief, peak expiratory flow, or FEV1
Heart rate and rhythm, particularly with high doses or cardiac disease
Serum potassium with frequent or nebulized high-dose use
Blood glucose in patients with diabetes
counsel: Use as a rescue inhaler for sudden breathing symptoms; carry it with you
If you need it more often than usual or it works less well, your asthma may be getting worse - contact your doctor
Shake and prime the inhaler as instructed; use a spacer if advised and rinse the device weekly
Some shakiness, fast heartbeat, or headache can occur and usually passes
Seek urgent help if breathing worsens right after a dose or if your usual dose does not relieve symptoms
pk: Bronchodilation within about 5 minutes of inhalation
Peak effect at approximately 30 minutes to 2 hours
Store at 25 C (77 F) with excursions 15-30 C; protect from heat; do not puncture or incinerate the canister
pearls: First-line quick-relief (rescue) bronchodilator; rapid onset within minutes
Frequent or increasing use is a key marker of poor asthma control and should prompt step-up of controller therapy
Can cause tremor, tachycardia, and transient hypokalemia, especially at high or nebulized doses
Prime a new or unused inhaler and shake before each actuation; spacer improves delivery
Non-selective beta-blockers antagonize its effect and can provoke bronchospasm
missed: Salbutamol is usually used as needed for symptoms rather than on a fixed schedule, so there is no missed dose. If prescribed before exercise or at set times and a dose is missed, use it when remembered unless it is nearly time for the next dose; do not double up.
overdose: Overdose can cause exaggerated beta-adrenergic effects: tachycardia, arrhythmias, tremor, hypertension or hypotension, hypokalemia, hyperglycemia, and seizures. Cardiac arrest and death may occur. Treatment is supportive; a cardioselective beta-blocker may be considered with caution in patients with bronchospasm. Contact Poison Control (1-800-222-1222).
